I want to take my time with this one, because the question deserves an answer that is not hurried. There are two things worth separating: what you asked, and what you would find useful once you have it. The first is narrow and I can answer it plainly. The second is larger, and it depends on what you are planning afterwards, which I do not know yet. So let me answer the narrow one first, and then tell me whether the larger one is where you actually wanted to go, and I will follow you there.

There is a longer answer here, and I would rather give it to you properly than compress it into a slogan. The short version is that the thing you are asking about has two halves that behave differently, and only one of them is under my control. The other half belongs to circumstances I can describe but cannot change, so the useful move is to make the first half as good as it can be and then check whether the second half still matters to you. If it does, tell me and we will look at it together rather than separately.

Let me walk through this slowly, because a hurried version of it would leave you with the impression that the answer is simpler than it is. First, the part you already know, restated so we are using the same words. Second, the part that surprised me when I looked closely, and why it changes what I would suggest. Third, what I would do next if it were mine, and what I would want to know before committing to that. Ask me to stop at any point and I will stop there instead of finishing for the sake of finishing.
